claims.title: Sinhalese settlement and the founding of Anuradhapura
claims.summary: By tradition Prince Vijaya's followers settle the island; the kingdom of Anuradhapura is founded under Pandukabhaya and grows into the strongest Sinhalese state, capital for over a thousand years.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-500bce-sinhalese-settlement-and-the-founding-of, claim TL:LKA:event:500bce:sinhalese-settlement-and-the-founding-of, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Buddhism introduced under Devanampiya Tissa
claims.summary: The missionary Mahinda, sent during the reign of the Mauryan emperor Ashoka, converts King Devanampiya Tissa near Mihintale, establishing Theravada Buddhism as the island's defining faith.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-250bce-buddhism-introduced-under-devanampiya-tissa, claim TL:LKA:event:250bce:buddhism-introduced-under-devanampiya-tissa, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Hydraulic civilisation and South Indian invasions
claims.summary: Anuradhapura's kings build vast reservoir-and-channel systems to irrigate the dry plain, while recurrent invasions from South India culminate in the Chola conquest and the abandonment of the capital around 1017.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-200bce-hydraulic-civilisation-and-south-indian, claim TL:LKA:event:200bce:hydraulic-civilisation-and-south-indian, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kassapa I builds Sigiriya
claims.summary: A king who took the throne by killing his father moves the capital to the summit of a 180-metre granite peak, entered through a stair rising from the mouth of a brick lion.

sources.label: Ancient City of Sigiriya (World Heritage List)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-477-kassapa-i-builds-sigiriya, claim TL:LKA:event:477:kassapa-i-builds-sigiriya, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Polonnaruwa becomes the capital
claims.summary: Following the Chola conquest and the abandonment of Anuradhapura, Polonnaruwa is established as Sri Lanka's second great capital in the north-central dry zone.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1017-polonnaruwa-becomes-the-capital, claim TL:LKA:event:1017:polonnaruwa-becomes-the-capital, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Golden age under Parakramabahu I
claims.summary: Parakramabahu I rebuilds the city and its irrigation, creating the immense Parakrama Samudra reservoir and a garden-capital that marks the high point of the Polonnaruwa period.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1153-golden-age-under-parakramabahu-i, claim TL:LKA:event:1153:golden-age-under-parakramabahu-i, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Decline and the drift southward
claims.summary: Invasion, the breakdown of the dry-zone irrigation system and disease lead to the abandonment of the northern capitals and the migration of Sinhalese power toward the south-west and the Kandyan hills.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1200-decline-and-the-drift-southward, claim TL:LKA:event:1200:decline-and-the-drift-southward, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Arrival of the Portuguese
claims.summary: A Portuguese fleet reaches Colombo, opening more than a century of Portuguese control over Ceylon's coasts and its profitable cinnamon trade.

sources.label: Sri Lanka: The Portuguese in Sri Lanka (1505–1658)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1505-arrival-of-the-portuguese, claim TL:LKA:event:1505:arrival-of-the-portuguese, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dutch supplant the Portuguese
claims.summary: Allied with Kandy, the Dutch East India Company takes Galle (1640) and expels the Portuguese with the fall of Colombo (1656) and Jaffna (1658), ruling the maritime provinces for cinnamon.

sources.label: Old Town of Galle and its Fortifications

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1658-dutch-supplant-the-portuguese, claim TL:LKA:event:1658:dutch-supplant-the-portuguese, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Britain takes the Dutch coasts
claims.summary: With the Netherlands under French control in Europe, Britain begins taking over the maritime provinces — the island changes hands as a consequence of a war fought elsewhere.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1796-britain-takes-the-dutch-coasts, claim TL:LKA:event:1796:britain-takes-the-dutch-coasts, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kandyan Convention unifies the island under Britain
claims.summary: The Kandyan chiefs cede the highland kingdom to the British crown, ending the last independent Sinhalese kingdom and placing the whole island under a single colonial administration.

sources.label: Path to Freedom: 1815 Convention and Dominion Status
sources.publisher: Department of National Archives, Sri Lanka

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1815-kandyan-convention-unifies-the-island-under, claim TL:LKA:event:1815:kandyan-convention-unifies-the-island-under, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Plantation economy and Tamil labour migration
claims.summary: British coffee and later tea estates transform the highlands; indentured South Indian Tamil labourers are brought in to work them, forming the Indian Tamil community of the plantation districts.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1840-plantation-economy-and-tamil-labour-migration, claim TL:LKA:event:1840:plantation-economy-and-tamil-labour-migration, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: One administration for the whole island
claims.summary: Reform dissolves the separate systems of the maritime provinces and the highlands, governing Ceylon as a single colony for the first time.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1833-one-administration-for-the-whole-island, claim TL:LKA:event:1833:one-administration-for-the-whole-island, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Universal suffrage and reform
claims.summary: Constitutional reforms grant universal adult suffrage in Ceylon, far ahead of most colonies, strengthening a moderate movement for self-government.

sources.label: Path to Freedom: 1815 Convention and Dominion Status
sources.publisher: Department of National Archives, Sri Lanka

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1931-universal-suffrage-and-reform, claim TL:LKA:event:1931:universal-suffrage-and-reform, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of the Dominion of Ceylon
claims.summary: Ceylon becomes an independent dominion within the Commonwealth as its 1947 constitution takes effect, with D. S. Senanayake as first prime minister.

sources.label: History of Sri Lanka: Independent Ceylon (1948–71)
Path to Freedom: 1815 Convention and Dominion Status
sources.publisher: Department of National Archives, Sri Lanka

sources.label: A Guide to the United States' History of Recognition: Sri Lanka
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1948-independence-of-the-dominion-of-ceylon, claim TL:LKA:event:1948:independence-of-the-dominion-of-ceylon, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Indian Tamil plantation workers disenfranchised
claims.summary: The estate workforce brought from South India is stripped of the vote a year after independence — the opening move of a nationalism that alienated the Tamil minority.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1949-indian-tamil-plantation-workers-disenfranchised, claim TL:LKA:event:1949:indian-tamil-plantation-workers-disenfranchised, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Ceylon becomes the Republic of Sri Lanka
claims.summary: A new republican constitution ends dominion status and changes the country's name from Ceylon to Sri Lanka, while it remains within the Commonwealth.

sources.label: History of Sri Lanka: Independent Ceylon (1948–71)
Sri Lanka: Reconstruction and the modern nation

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1972-ceylon-becomes-the-republic-of-sri-lanka, claim TL:LKA:event:1972:ceylon-becomes-the-republic-of-sri-lanka, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Sinhala Only Act
claims.summary: S. W. R. D. Bandaranaike is elected on a wave of Sinhalese nationalism and makes Sinhala the sole official language, alongside measures elevating Buddhism.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1956-the-sinhala-only-act, claim TL:LKA:event:1956:the-sinhala-only-act, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The JVP insurrection
claims.summary: A Marxist rising is put down; its missing would still be uncounted in the state's own figures forty-five years later.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1971-the-jvp-insurrection, claim TL:LKA:event:1971:the-jvp-insurrection, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The LTTE is founded
claims.summary: The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam form to fight for Tamil rights, seven years before the war that would define them.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1976-the-ltte-is-founded, claim TL:LKA:event:1976:the-ltte-is-founded, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Civil war between the state and the LTTE
claims.summary: After the anti-Tamil violence of Black July in 1983, the LTTE fights for a separate Tamil state; the war ends with the group's military defeat in May 2009 after about twenty-six years.

sources.label: Sri Lanka: Reconstruction and the modern nation

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1983-civil-war-between-the-state-and-the-ltte, claim TL:LKA:event:1983:civil-war-between-the-state-and-the-ltte, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Indo-Lanka accords and the Indian peacekeepers
claims.summary: Accords create new councils for the Tamil north and east and bring in an Indian peacekeeping force, which spends three years bogged down in the fighting it came to end.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1987-the-indo-lanka-accords-and-the-indian, claim TL:LKA:event:1987:the-indo-lanka-accords-and-the-indian, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Indian withdrawal and the expulsion of northern Muslims
claims.summary: Indian troops leave and the war escalates; the LTTE expels thousands of Muslims from the northern districts.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-1990-indian-withdrawal-and-the-expulsion-of-northern, claim TL:LKA:event:1990:indian-withdrawal-and-the-expulsion-of-northern, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Indian Ocean tsunami
claims.summary: Waves from a magnitude-9.1 undersea earthquake off Sumatra devastate Sri Lanka's coasts, killing more than 30,000 people in the country's deadliest natural disaster.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-2004-indian-ocean-tsunami, claim TL:LKA:event:2004:indian-ocean-tsunami, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Economic crisis and sovereign default
claims.summary: A foreign-exchange crisis forces Sri Lanka's first sovereign default; shortages and protests topple President Gotabaya Rajapaksa, leading to an IMF bailout and, in 2024, the election of Anura Kumara Dissanayake.

sources.label: Sri Lanka: Reconstruction and the modern nation

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-2022-economic-crisis-and-sovereign-default, claim TL:LKA:event:2022:economic-crisis-and-sovereign-default, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The state counts its missing
claims.summary: The government acknowledges for the first time that some 65,000 people are missing from the 26-year war and the 1971 insurrection.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-2016-the-state-counts-its-missing, claim TL:LKA:event:2016:the-state-counts-its-missing, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Easter Sunday bombings
claims.summary: Jihadist suicide bombers attack churches and hotels, killing more than 350 people.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Sri Lanka: From the hydraulic kingdoms of Anuradhapura to an island republic.", terralore.co/country/LKA/chronicle#ev-2019-the-easter-sunday-bombings, claim TL:LKA:event:2019:the-easter-sunday-bombings, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
